messages:
alex_green: noticing a sustained 5xx spike from customers hitting hosted inference in us-east-3 (AZ b/c). started ~06:12 UTC, ~3x baseline 502/504s :rotating_light:

maria_nguyen: confirmed in the dashboard — gateway timeouts and a few TLS handshake failures. per-route error % looks concentrated on api-hosted-us-east-3 cluster.

samir_kapoor: +1 on spike. packet retransmit count up on the AZ b links. traceroutes show one hop in transit provider returning high latency/missed packets.

jen_support: customer X reported repeated "timeout waiting for response" and then billing hits from retries. opened ticket PROD-11248 and grouped logs.

net-monitor-bot: alert: egress-loss(us-east-3b) > 1.8% for 10m; BGP flaps observed for ASN 64512 -> withdraw/announce pattern.

alex_green: can we confirm any recent config pushes in that AZ? autoscaler, nginx changes?

maria_nguyen: no infra pushes in the window. control-plane deploys none. only thing is a provider-side maintenance we didn't opt into (carrier ticket 8741).

samir_kapoor: quick repro suggestion for SREs: run this from one of the affected hosts and collect pcap + mtr:

```
# on host in us-east-3b
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/egress-us-east-3b.pcap -s 0 host <provider-hop-ip> and port 443
mtr -z -c 100 <customer-ip> > /tmp/mtr-egress.txt
```

jen_support: i'm patching customers with a temporary suggestion: set client retry backoff to 2s->10s and enable client-side idempotency where possible. Sending update to affected accounts now.

alex_green: paths look lossy, recommend immediate traffic steering to us-east-2 (same region but different provider fabric) for critical customers via routing policy. Can we trigger a fast failover?

maria_nguyen: routing policy executed: shifting 40% of new traffic to us-east-2 for model endpoints behind hosted-inference-us-east. Watch for cache miss penalty.

samir_kapoor: also verify MTU mismatch — signs of fragmentation seen in some logs. ran:

```sh
ip link show dev eth0
# expect MTU 9001 for jumbo frames; if <1500, may cause fragmentation on provider path
```

jen_support: CS: customers on smaller instances seeing more timeouts; escalated to premium customers and offered API retries update and credits for the event window.

net-monitor-bot: note: BGP flap stabilized 06:28 UTC after provider performed partial reroute; egress-loss dropped to 0.6% but error rates still above normal.

alex_green: next steps: (1) keep traffic steering active for 60m, (2) collect pcaps + MTRs for provider handoff, (3) engage provider NOC with pcap and AS path history, (4) create post-incident action items (routing guardrails, auto-failover runbook).

maria_nguyen: i'm creating an incident page and attaching graphs + the customer list. link: https://console.redwood.internal/incidents/6109876543 (private).

samir_kapoor: added a short firewall check — discovered one egress ACL had an accidental rate-limit to the transit prefix (rule created during testing left enabled). disabling it reduced tail latency for some hosts.

jen_support: noted: billing team queued invoice hold for impacted customers during window. updating support threads.

alex_green: thanks team. I'll follow up with provider NOC ticket webrtc-112244 and schedule a postmortem. For now keep monitoring and update this thread with pcaps. :eyes:

maria_nguyen: attaching initial MTR + summary in the incident page. will add pcap when available.

samir_kapoor: pcap uploaded to /artifacts/6109876543/egress-us-east-3b.pcap — shared with provider NOC.

jen_support: closing loop with customer X — they confirmed timeouts decreased after our traffic steering. still watching.

net-monitor-bot: follow-up alert threshold lowered to 0.5% to catch regressions.

alex_green: last note: add a canary that simulates large-requests pattern (long seq lengths) to catch similar degradation earlier.

jen_support: will capture action items into the incident doc and ping owners. :white_check_mark:
